intro.title: Write pick generic with keyof
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom utility function called `myPick` that selects specific properties from an object. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's `keyof` operator to create a type-safe generic function that works with any object type. The main concepts involve generics, type constraints, and indexed access types to ensure the function returns only the requested keys. This exercise will help you understand how to write reusable, type-safe utilities in TypeScript.
intro.usecase: The `Pick` utility type is essential for creating type-safe, reusable components in large-scale applications. For example, when building a user profile dashboard, you might have a full `User` interface but only need to display a subset of fields like `name` and `email` in a summary panel. Using `Pick<User, 'name' | 'email'>` ensures your component only accepts the required properties, preventing bugs and improving maintainability. This pattern is also common in form libraries, API response filtering, and configuration objects where you need to select specific properties from a larger type.
